You can track issues and tasks here: GitHub Project Board: View on GitHub 1 Introduction Introduction Text 1.1 Purpose The purpose of this project is to replicate analysis done by the HEYA Research Group for natural disasters on points of interest across Canada. 1.2 Required Information 1.2.1 Datasets This tutorial uses the following publicly available datasets: Data Provider Dataset Type Natural Resources Canada (CFS / CWFIS) National Burned Area Composite (NBAC) wildfire perimeters (1972–2024) (cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca) Polygon (vector) Natural Resources Canada (EGS) Floods in Canada - Archive (flood extent products) (open.canada.ca) Polygon (vector) Environment and Climate Change Canada Historical climate observations & station metadata (climate.weather.gc.ca) Point (vector) National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration - National Hurricane Center NHC GIS Archive (nhc.noaa.gov) Point & Polygon (vector) Statistics Canada Open Database of Hospital Facilities (open.canada.ca) Point (vector)   This tutorial also uses datasets with access restrictions. Access may require institutional access, and/or data-use agreements. Data Provider Dataset Access Statistics Canada Postal Code Conversion File (PCCF) v7E Licensed Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE) Local Climate Zones & PM2.5 (smoke) by Postcode Request via project creation in CANUE (free) 1.2.2 R packages The following R packages are required to run the code in this book: Data processing and wrangling dplyr tidyverse tidyr lubridate data.table tibble readr purrr stringr readxl writexl rvest httr fs tm SnowballC proxy cmdstanr arrow sfarrow Data visualization and mapping ggplot2 maps knitr kableExtra terra Spatial analysis sf geosphere mapview Data download weathercan Optional furrr (offers improved processing speeds) The following code installs (if needed) and loads these packages: # Vector of required packages packages <- c( "dplyr", "tidyr", "lubridate", "data.table", "tibble", "readr", "purrr", "furrr", "stringr", "readxl", "writexl", "ggplot2", "maps", "rvest", "httr", "tm", "SnowballC", "proxy", "cmdstanr", "sf", "geosphere", "fs", "knitr", "kableExtra", "arrow", "sfarrow", "weathercan", "furrr", "tidyverse", "terra", "mapview" ) # Install any that are missing installed <- rownames(installed.packages()) to_install <- setdiff(packages, installed) if (length(to_install) > 0) { install.packages(to_install) } # Load all packages invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE)) #configure mapview to use public imagery mapviewOptions(basemaps = c("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"))
